text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: P0 — Cross-region routing anomaly: sudden p90 latency spike and 502/504s for EU->US customer requests. Auto-detected by routing-health (alerts).
Mia: I'm oncall for infra, ack. Paging Ram (network) and Katie (routing). Anyone seeing matching errors in other regions? :eyes:
Ram: Ack. I see packet loss increase between eu1 and us-east transit at the edge load-balancer layer. BGP paths look ok but latency is spiking. Src: eu1 customers -> us services.
Katie: Ack. Graphs show a routing policy rollout at 22:17 UTC that added a latency-based steer variant. It looks like the new policy has a flapping preference for us-east when p50 crosses 120ms.
Mia: Can we confirm policy change commit id? Katie?
Katie: Yes, commit ab3f2c0 introduced the adaptive-latency-steer rule. Recent canary showed weird oscillation on low-traffic prefixes. Here's the rule snippet:
```
policy "adaptive-latency-steer" {
  match: region == "eu" && path_latency > 120ms
  action: steer_to("us-east", weight=80)
  cooldown: 30s
}
```
Sam: I see on the request logs a loop where requests are steered to us-east, then fallback to eu1 due to local overload, then re-steered — causing request amplification and retries. 5xxs align with that pattern.
Mia: Root cause hypothesis: the new steer rule's cooldown too short + inaccurate latency signal caused oscillation and overload on us-east, amplifying retries across regions.
Ram: Network teams confirm transient packet drops at eu1 egress to inter-region fabric. Might have lowered throughput so us-east instances were briefly overloaded.
Mia: Immediate mitigation plan:
1) Katie — rollback adaptive-latency-steer to previous policy (ab3f2c0 revert) or disable for eu->us flows. (ETA 2m)
2) Ram — put a soft rate-limit on cross-region steering at egress to dampen churn. (ETA 3m)
3) Sam — enable request-level de-dup/time-window retry guard in edge proxy for eu->us paths. (ETA 5m)
4) Mia — notify oncall handoff and CS if customer-impacting. (ETA now)
Katie: Rolling back now. `configctl rollback --policy adaptive-latency-steer --to=ab11a8d` — applying. Will watch rollout.
deploy-bot: deploy started for config rollback (change_id cfg-3892). Canary 0/5 -> 3/5 -> 5/5.
Katie: Rollback completed, routing weights back to stable profile. Monitoring.
Sam: Enabled retry guard on edge: `edgectl set retry-window --path eu->us --ms 2000` — reduced duplicate requests.
Ram: Applied egress soft rate-limit for cross-region pins: `netpol apply cross-region-eu-throttle=600rps`.
Mia: Initial numbers — p90 latency for eu->us dropped from ~420ms to ~180ms in 4 minutes, 5xxs down 78% vs peak. Still above baseline; continuing to monitor.
CS-Bot: Notifying CS triage: several customers in EU reported higher error rates, marking impacted tenants: acme-co, finlytics, shopqube. Draft message prepared.
Katie: Confirming load on us-east edge dropped after rollback. No errors on service-owned instances themselves (app-level 200s), this was routing-layer induced.
Sam: Logs show a small burst of retries from eu proxies during the oscillation — we should add a guard in the routing agent to prevent re-steering within 60s of a previous steering decision.
Mia: Good call. Add as action item. For now, I've documented mitigation steps in the incident runbook and will escalate to 2nd oncall for a longer-term fix.
Mia: Handoff to Ingrid for continued monitoring/communication. Ingrid — I'm leaving a short summary and suggested next steps in the postmortem template.
Ingrid: Taking over. Thanks @Mia. I'll keep watch for 60m and coordinate a postmortem. Questions for follow-up:
- Add hysteresis to adaptive-latency-steer (increase cooldown to 300s), and require sustained p50/p90 trend for 5m before steer.
- Rate-limit steered traffic at egress and introduce per-customer caps for cross-region bursts.
- Add a synthetic that checks for steering oscillation pattern.
Ram: Network ops follow-ups: check fabric retransmit/backpressure patterns between eu1 and us-edge provider, confirm no hardware flaps.
Katie: We'll create a rollback-safe feature flag for adaptive steer so future canary failures auto-disable before full rollout.
Mia: Customer-impact assessment: ~5% of EU traffic affected at peak, top affected tenants listed by CS. No data loss, only transient errors/latency. Will prepare timeline.
Ingrid: I'll open the incident postmortem and tag owners: Katie (routing policy), Ram (network), Sam (edge proxy), Mia (oncall coordination). ETA initial postmortem draft: 48h.
Mia: Thanks team. If anything regresses, re-alert on this thread. :thumbsup:
Ingrid: Logging final note: mitigation succeeded, rollback stable, continuing observation. Closing handoff at 22:42 UTC.
